title: Sixty years, 37 moments
lede: From a Dallas coffee shop to a hotel in Minnesota. Filter by thread.

events.title: Brinker comes to Dallas
events.text: After leaving Jack in the Box, Norman Brinker opens a coffee shop called Brink’s.

events.title: The first Steak and Ale
events.text: It opens near Lemmon and Oak Lawn avenues in Dallas. A local news site gives the day as February 26.

events.title: Public company
events.text: Steak and Ale goes public with 28 restaurants.

events.title: The alumni start arriving
events.text: Tim Gannon and Chris Sullivan, later founders of Outback Steakhouse, are working at the Steak and Ale in Rockville, Maryland.

events.title: Merger with Pillsbury
events.text: The chain has 109 restaurants in 24 states. Brinker becomes a Pillsbury executive vice president and director.

events.title: The first Bennigan’s
events.text: Brinker develops a second concept inside the same company.

events.title: Chairman of S&A
events.text: Brinker, president of S&A Restaurant Corp. since February 1966, becomes its chairman and chief executive.

events.title: Head of Pillsbury’s restaurants
events.text: Brinker becomes president of the Pillsbury Restaurant Group and chairman of Burger King.

events.title: Bennigan’s gets the growth
events.text: Pillsbury says Bennigan’s has 66 restaurants in 16 states and will have 108 by May.

events.title: Brinker leaves
events.text: He resigns from S&A and Pillsbury and takes over Chili’s that September.

events.title: Jenkins goes to Friday’s
events.text: J. Michael Jenkins leaves S&A to become president of T.G.I. Friday’s. A reference history says he later tried to buy S&A.

events.title: Pillsbury reviews its restaurants
events.text: After a nine-month review it says it will reduce the division. Steak and Ale’s chairman leaves.

events.title: Grand Met buys Pillsbury
events.text: The British group pays $5.68 billion and promises to sell the restaurants that serve liquor.

events.title: $431 million buyout
events.text: Grand Met agrees to sell 159 Steak and Ale and 221 Bennigan’s restaurants to management, D.J.S./Inverness and Citicorp.

events.title: Metromedia
events.text: Reference histories and the Dallas Observer date John Kluge’s acquisition of S&A to this year. We found no contemporary report of the terms.

events.title: Kaufman arrives
events.text: Kluge puts Michael Kaufman, an acquisitions specialist, in charge of his steakhouse company.

events.title: 107 steakhouses
events.text: A company release counts 107 Steak and Ale restaurants in 24 states. Bob Mandes is the chain’s president.

events.title: Spae takes operations
events.text: Bill Spae becomes chief operating officer of Steak and Ale, and later its president.

events.title: For sale
events.text: Metromedia agrees to sell Steak and Ale, with 66 locations, and its Ponderosa and Bonanza chains to APEX, keeping Bennigan’s.

events.title: Managed, not sold
events.text: APEX’s principals take over management of all four chains instead. Kaufman steps down.

events.title: Another chief executive
events.text: Metromedia Restaurant Group names Vince Runco chief executive.

events.title: Dover quits
events.text: Clay Dover, chief executive for about six months, resigns over the “strategic direction” of the company.

events.title: Lenders
events.text: The Wall Street Journal reports a breach of lending agreements with GE Capital Solutions. The company says it is not preparing a bankruptcy filing.

events.title: Chapter 7
events.text: S&A Restaurant Corp. and affiliates file 38 petitions in Sherman, Texas. All 58 Steak and Ale restaurants and about 150 company-owned Bennigan’s close.

events.title: Gone everywhere
events.text: A Michigan news site reports the Plymouth restaurant among the 58 closed nationwide.

events.title: Atalaya buys the names
events.text: The private-equity firm says it is buying both brands and their trademarks. Metromedia’s other steakhouse unit files for Chapter 11.

events.title: Norman Brinker dies
events.text: He is 78. Brinker International then has about 1,700 restaurants.

events.title: A grocery licence
events.text: The Dallas Observer reports a deal to put Steak and Ale and Bennigan’s dishes in supermarkets.

events.title: Mangiamele
events.text: Paul Mangiamele becomes chief executive of Bennigan’s Franchising Co., which also holds Steak and Ale.

events.title: The reunion
events.text: About 400 former employees meet in Dallas; 55 sponsors paid $105,000 for the party.

events.title: The estate’s leftovers
events.text: Oak Point Partners buys the remnant assets of the S&A bankruptcy estate, case no. 08-41898.

events.title: Legendary Restaurant Brands
events.text: Paul and Gwen Mangiamele buy the franchisor and trademarks from Fortress Investment Group. Terms are not disclosed.

events.title: A Mexican agreement
events.text: Legendary announces a master development agreement for Mexico. No Steak and Ale there appears on its 2026 locations page.

events.title: Back on a menu
events.text: Three Steak and Ale dishes, the Kensington Club among them, are added at Bennigan’s.

events.title: The Endeavor deal
events.text: A 15-restaurant agreement with Endeavor Properties names Burnsville, Minnesota as the first site.

events.title: Burnsville opens
events.text: The first new Steak and Ale in 16 years opens beside a Wyndham hotel.

events.title: A second is announced
events.text: Former employees John and Dixie Benca plan a franchised restaurant in Anderson, South Carolina for early 2027.
